Titan warning is wrong: Titan requires identical union types; 6.3.2.4 EXAMPLE 1 shows U1<->U2 assignment as valid.

Source union has a default alternative d whose name also exists in the target; first rule gives {d:={i:=1}}, the default rule would give {i:=1}. Titan resolves the default alternative first (expects UA instead of UC), i.e. violates this requirement. The target-has-default direction cannot produce an ambiguity because of 6.2.5 restriction a) (distinct effective fields).

Ambiguity: reading that both default-alternative rules are fallbacks. Test: first rule fails (alternative d is charstring in target), fallback union-to-arbitrary rule yields {i:=1}. Titan warning: Titan does not implement union structural compatibility.
Log output format is not standardised; the test uses any2unistr (defined to equal the log output) and checks it differs from the log string of the plain boolean value true.

Positive reading of the NOTE: an unconstrained anytype accepts a value of a list-constrained anytype. The incompatibility case is covered by the reject-like EXAMPLE only. Titan warning: anytype fields need a Titan extension attribute.
